newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-INJURY-HIT SCOTLAND CALL UP REINFORCEMENTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INJURY-HIT SCOTLAND CALL UP REINFORCEMENTS.

text.p: Scotland manager Craig Brown moved to solve his problems for the World Cup qualifiers against Latvia and Estonia by calling up in-form pair Dougie Freedman of Crystal Palace and Bolton's John McGinlay on Thursday.
The two strikers will join the squad before they fly out on Friday for the Group four qualifiers against Latvia on Saturday and Estonia next Wednesday.
But Brown, who has lost the services of Gordon Durie, Ally McCoist and Kevin Gallacher, suggested that neither Freedman nor McGinlay would start the game in Latvia on Saturday afternoon.

He said: "I am very excited about the prospect of them joining the squad because I know their capabilities, but when it comes to the starting line-up neither player will jump ahead of those who were here originally."
Brown is looking to win both games in an effort to keep the pressure on Sweden who head the group.
"A 0-0 draw or narrow defeat would please Estonia whereas Latvia will try to come and score," he said.
"They are totally different in shape, style and attitude, so we have to approach each game differently.
"We will get a more open game against Latvia which gives us a chance to score, but at the same time they will also be a threat going forward."
